title: Counting Sort Preconditions
statement: Let the machine limits be a word bound, a space bound, and a depth bound, let $�$ be a memory map from natural-number addresses to integers, and let $A$ specify a number $n$ of items, source and destination addresses, key-address parameters, a key bound $nb$, and a counter region. For every $i<n$, the source address contains item $it(i)$; the key of that item is stored at an address within memory, outside the destination and counter regions, and that address contains $kf(i)$, where $kf(i)<nb$. The space bound is at most the word bound; the source, destination, and counter regions (of length $nb+1$) fit in memory and are pairwise disjoint; and the key address of each item lies outside both the destination and counter regions.

each key address lies outside the destination region
each key address lies outside the counter region
caveat: The statement depends on the omitted definitions of the key-address calculation and of region disjointness/outside. The memory map is denoted by μ; it was accidentally rendered as an empty symbol above.
